title: Agents and Tokens: Multi-Agent Autonomous Reasoning over a Hydrodynamic Token Store
abstract: arXiv:2605.01102v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models and the agents built on them are the most capable reasoning machines ever built, and science is beginning to put them to work. Atmospheric and oceanic sciences are starting to see agentic integration, but coastal hydrodynamics remains largely untouched by AI. Simply, agents cannot easily read its data products without saturating their context windows. A time frame from a coastal model can hold hundreds of megabytes, and if the archive's chunking does not suit the query, the agent will spend more time downloading and compacting than gaining insights. After all, the archives were designed for storage, not for the fast, on-the-fly access agents need. Speech and music once hit the same wall. translated_title: 智能体与词元：基于水动力词元存储库的多智能体自主推理
translated_abstract: 大语言模型以及构建在其上的智能体是有史以来最强大的推理机器，科学界正开始让它们投入实际工作。大气与海洋科学领域已开始出现智能体化的集成应用，但近岸水动力学领域基本上仍未受到人工智能的影响。简而言之，智能体难以在不耗尽其上下文窗口的情况下读取该领域的数据产品。近岸模型的一个时间片段可能包含数百兆字节的数据，如果存档的分块方式不适合查询需求，智能体将花费更多时间在下载和压缩数据上，而不是获取科学洞察。毕竟，这些存档是为存储而设计的，并非为智能体所需的快速即时访问而设计。语音和音乐领域曾经也遇到过同样的障碍。一分钟的音频包含数百万个数字，但如今的音频模型却能够进行对话并创作音乐。它们通过“聆听”词元（token）“学会”了做到这一点。神经音频编解码器将波形转换为离散符号的短序列（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文受神经音频编解码器将波形转化为离散词元的启发，提出将近岸水动力模型的海量数据转化为离散词元存储库，使多智能体系统能够在不饱和上下文窗口的前提下对该数据进行自主推理与分析。
en_tdlr: Inspired by neural audio codecs that convert waveforms into discrete tokens, this paper proposes a hydrodynamic token store that transforms massive coastal model data into discrete token representations, enabling multi-agent systems to autonomously reason over the data without saturating their context windows.
